newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: REUTERS LAUNCHES BALTIC NEWS SERVICE.
newsitem.headline: REUTERS LAUNCHES BALTIC NEWS SERVICE.

text.p: Reuters will today launch in Lithuania the Reuters Baltic News (RBN) service, a real time financial news service covering the Baltic countries' financial markets.
Seven journalists will cover the equity, capital and foreign exchange markets of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania.
"We are looking forward to being the main provider of financial information to the Baltic countries," said Simon Haydon, Reuters' bureau chief for the Nordic and Baltic countries.
The new service, produced in English, is the latest expansion to more than 50 national news services provided by Reuters around the world.
These services are an addition to Reuters traditional international news service which cover 160 countries with over 1,500 journalists.
The Reuters Baltic News service will cover all news that is important to the Baltics financial markets including politics, industry and trade relationships.
"Our journalists will work by the high standards set by Reuters over the last 150 years around the world to give our Baltic clients what they need," Haydon said.
"The emphasis will be on fast, accurate information vital for the Baltic financial markets."
Reuters set up its first operations in the Baltics in 1994, opening offices in Tallinn and Riga, as part of the company's Nordic network. It opened its first office in Lithuania in 1995.
Reuters was first active in the Baltic states from the 1920s.
RBN was launched in Estonia on Tuesday this week and in Latvia on Wednesday.
